mentl/2660e1f:
mentl2 (wheel src/parser.mn compiled by seed) diverged from the seed
parser on the resume-with-state form, blocking pass-3 at the FIRST
handler arm using `resume() with field = expr` (src/backends/wasm.mn:76,
the wat_to_string handler) — 8038 cascading parse errors → broken AST
→ lower_expr_body unreachable trap.

Two convergent root causes, both seed-grounded:

C1: parse_resume shared parse_handler_state_fields across two contexts
with DIFFERENT termination grammars. Handler-decl state ends at TLBrace
(comma always a field separator). Resume-state-update ends when a comma
is NOT followed by `IDENT =` — the comma is then the match-arm
separator. The shared fn recursed unconditionally on TComma, eating the
arm separator + the next arm`s name. Fix: separate
parse_resume_state_updates with the seed`s exact lookahead predicate
(bootstrap/src/parser_compound.wat $parse_resume_state_updates — the
arbiter, pass-2 proves it). Separate fn, not a context flag (mirrors
the seed`s two-function split; drift 8 refused). Same {name,init}
record shape (drift 7 refused).

C2: with C1 correctly orphaning the arm-separator comma,
parse_handler_arms` skip_sep (only `;`/newline) could not skip it.
The seed`s $parse_handler_arms skips an optional TComma between arms;
the wheel`s canonical sibling parse_match_arms already does
(skip_ws → optional TComma → skip_ws). Converged parse_handler_arms to
that idiom — handler arms separate identically to match arms (the
seed`s own comment asserts this mirror). Restores consistency.

Also includes the prior parse_resume bare-`resume()` fix
(Hβ.parser.resume-no-arg, SYNTAX.md:766-777).

Empirical: pass-2 intact (1978 fns = +1 parse_resume_state_updates,
valid WASM, no regression). Pass-3 first divergence advances

#135/#138). B1-B4 micro-tests parse clean in rebuilt mentl2.

from the stores she already owns and writes nothing back: blooms
witnessed by month, notes touched in the year (at is last-touched, and
the heading says so), the whole garden — kept and placed, one set — on
the bloom wheel with the visitor-coverage line under it, every yard's

section, and always prints the light paper — the dark palette lives on

year in review. BloomCalendar gains the garden context; Kept links to
Print the year beside Save a copy.
noodles/26087a8:
Two halves of the same complaint. The mixer's state existed twice —
mixState in main.js, channelState in audio.js — pushed one way by
applyTrackMix and never read back, while devices already ran the other
way round (audio.patch is the read, setPatch the write). Two conventions
for two halves of the same engine, and a drift already sitting in them:
"send off" was -60 in the engine and -30 in the UI, neither wrong enough
to hear, because sendGain calls anything at or under -29 silence.

The mixer now follows the devices' convention. channelState is the one
copy; audio.mix(track) is the read and the strip paints from it rather
than from a handle it holds; MIX_DEFAULTS and the fader range live with
the channels they drive; setMix/resetMix are the bulk writes a vibe
roll, a project load and an undo all go through. What "muted" means once
solo is in play is stated once as trackMuted — the channel gates, the
grid's dimming, the session-record mute lane and renderOffline's
audible() had each been spelling it out for themselves.

That convention is also why undo was wrong. The dice writes three trees
(song, four device patches, the sends) and a snapshot cloned the song
alone, so one undo handed back the old song playing through the new
instruments in the new space — the headline gesture with a half-working
undo, on the exact stroke the cold open's safety rests on. A snapshot is
now { song, mix, devices }. The master bus stays out per D22. Ordinary
edits pay nothing: restoreSnap diffs each engine tree and only re-pushes
a track that actually moved, so undoing a note costs what it did before.
restoreSnap also deletes song keys before assigning, so undoing a roll
can't leave a dropped key (a dare, a laneNudge) behind.
